items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: He did most of the orchestra work, played with Pierron

ctx.x: And Leo, he wasn't much of a street man.

Leo was a good street man at the time because the brass band he played with had the music, you see, and he could read anything they put up there. And that's why Shawnee Neen was crazy about him. But he didn't play too much brass band work. Mostly he played like with Shawnee Neen, you know, and brass bands like that. He did most of the orchestra work, played with Pierron, you know, and had the band they made up around there, the band there. And he played with Rizzly Tuxedo when I was playing with him. And he…
Well, what trumpet player plays Sid now, much which or not?

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: then P-ron changed his band around where he went with P-ron

ctx.x: How old was your brother? Well he should be 49. 49. Yeah. And well he, they had a very good band and then from that, then P-ron changed his band around where he went with P-ron. And well he used to come home at night and just like he'd make his money, put it on the dresser, and even I come in when I put half of mine. Well I mean my mother never, you know, wants to do it but he just did it. Was there anybody else in your family that played your mother?
Did she play anything? No, my mother didn't play, but my mother could sing well.
